questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 85°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
questions.why: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the answer is 85°, not the co-interior supplement (95°).

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Who speaks the prologue in Romeo and Juliet?
questions.why: The Chorus delivers the 14-line prologue that sets up the whole story before the action begins.

questions.subject: History
questions.why: Continuity means aspects of life stay the same over time, while change describes what is different — historians look for both, not just dramatic events.

questions.subject: English
questions.why: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564, though he later worked mainly in London's theatres.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Act 1 Scene 1, who tries to stop the servants' street brawl?
questions.why: Benvolio draws his sword only to try to stop the fight, showing his peacemaking role, before Tybalt escalates it.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: What does 'mental health' actually refer to?
questions.why: Mental health means a person's overall emotional and psychological wellbeing, not just the presence of a diagnosed illness.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: Which statement about mental health is a common myth?
questions.why: This is a harmful myth — mental health struggles affect people regardless of strength or character.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: What is a healthy way to deal with strong emotions?
questions.why: Naming and sharing feelings with a trusted person helps process emotions, unlike suppressing or ignoring them.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In film music, what is a 'leitmotif'?
questions.why: A leitmotif is a short recurring musical idea linked to a character, place, or idea throughout a film.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In the key of C major, which chord is 'vi' in the I–vi–IV–V progression?
questions.why: In C major, the vi chord built on the sixth note (A) is A minor, giving the progression its sadder colour.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In song structure, what usually contrasts with the verse?
questions.why: The chorus contrasts with the verse in melody and lyrics, giving the song its catchy, repeated highlight.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: Globalisation mainly describes what happening between countries?
questions.why: Globalisation refers to countries becoming more connected through trade, culture, and technology, not less.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests how the amount of water poured onto plants affects plant height, using the same type of water each time. What is the controlled variable here?
questions.why: The controlled variable is kept the same on purpose, like the type of water — the amount of water is the independent variable, and height is the dependent variable.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In medieval times, why could the Church punish people even kings feared?
questions.why: The Church could excommunicate people, cutting them off from salvation, which even kings feared — a powerful spiritual weapon beyond royal control.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 58°. What is the corresponding angle on the other line?
questions.why: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel, so the matching angle is also 58°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has angles of 40°, 40°, and 100°. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: Two equal angles (40° and 40°) mean two equal sides, making this an isosceles triangle.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What causes a tsunami after an undersea earthquake?
questions.answer: Sudden movement of the sea floor
questions.why: A tsunami is triggered when a sudden shift in the sea floor during an earthquake displaces huge volumes of water.
options: Sudden movement of the sea floor

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What is the key difference between a long-term cause and a short-term (trigger) cause?
questions.answer: Long-term causes build up over years
questions.why: Long-term causes develop gradually over time, while a trigger (short-term) cause is the immediate event that sets things off.
options: Long-term causes build up over years
